problems.comment:
The new snow and wind slabs of the last few days are in some cases still prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches, including large ones. 
 As the day progresses as a consequence of new snow and wind there will be an appreciable increase in the avalanche danger. In the afternoon natural avalanches are to be expected. This applies in particular on north and east facing slopes. 
 Backcountry touring calls for extensive experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.
As a consequence of the rain wet and gliding avalanches are to be expected. Mostly these are medium-sized.

bulletin.snowpack: The new and wind-drifted snow from this week is stabilizing. With further snowfall and an increasingly strong westerly wind, wind slabs will form at elevated altitudes as the day progresses. Below 2000 m the snowpack will be weakened by warmth and rain.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
Avalanches can be released, even by a single winter sport participant. Natural avalanches are to be expected. These can also be triggered in the old snowpack, especially on north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m. In the typical avalanche paths the avalanches can in isolated cases reach very large size and endanger transportation routes situated at relatively high altitudes. 
 The conditions are very critical for backcountry touring.
Wet-snow avalanches
On steep grassy slopes medium-sized gliding avalanches are to be expected below approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

bulletin.snowpack:
The large amounts of new and wind-drifted snow from this week are stabilising. With renewed snowfall and an increasingly strong westerly wind, wind slabs will form at elevated altitudes as the day progresses. Below 2000 m the snowpack will be weakened by warmth and rain.
On north- and east-facing slopes above approximately 2600 m there is, in some places, coarse-grained old snow at the snow base. Due to being covered by large amounts of new and wind-drifted snow, it can scarcely be triggered anymore.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
150 to 250 cm of snow fell in the last eight days above approximately 2200 m. A large number of natural avalanches are to be expected, even large ones. In isolated cases avalanches can also be triggered in near-ground layers and reach very large size. This applies in particular on north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m. In the typical avalanche paths the avalanches can reach as far as the valley bottom and endanger transportation routes that are exposed. 
 The conditions are very dangerous for backcountry touring.
Wet-snow avalanches
On steep grassy slopes medium-sized gliding avalanches are to be expected below approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.
